what: You hear a short sentence once. Then you say it back exactly as you heard it.
tests: Listening and speaking: holding a sentence in memory and repeating it clearly.

scoring.note: Pearson's page lists these scored traits.

strategy: Listen for the meaning of the whole sentence, not single words.
Split the sentence into two or three chunks in your mind (who, does what, when or where).
Start speaking as soon as the tone sounds, while the sentence is fresh.
Copy the speaker's rhythm and intonation.
If you forget a word, keep going with the rest of the sentence.
example_prompt: The science building will be closed for repairs until the end of March.

strong.answer: The science building will be closed for repairs until the end of March.
strong.why: Every word is correct and it is said smoothly with natural stress.

medium.answer: The science building will be closed for repair until the end of the March.
medium.why: Most words are right; two small changes ('repair', 'the March') lower content a little.

weak.why: Many words are missing and there are long pauses and fillers.

mistakes: Trying to remember every single word instead of the meaning.
Stopping when one word is forgotten.
